summary: Iteration 9 — Frontend-only review of the 'Instagram-vibe' pivot (Stories, Explore, Hashtag pages, double-tap-to-like, Auto badge, bottom-nav swap). Registered two users via /api/auth/progressive-signup + /api/auth/complete-profile, seeded a post with '#test #networkcapital' + a story, then exercised the UI using token injection into localStorage. All 5 backend sanity endpoints return 200. All 11 frontend flows pass — no critical bugs found in the new work.
critical_code_review_comments: FeedPage.js is now ~485 lines with FeedPage + PostCard + modals in one file. Approaching the 700-line guideline; consider splitting PostCard into its own component file and moving the Create Post modal into components/CreatePostModal.js for maintainability.

StoriesRibbon.js: after a successful story upload load() is called but the toast says '+5' while the backend has not been verified to actually award the points from the UI flow. Minor — copy should match the backend contract.

FeedPage.handleMediaTap uses a 300ms double-tap window but also wires both onClick + onDoubleClick to the same handler. Works (the 2nd click within 300ms fires onDoubleClick AND the 2nd synthetic onClick, and the lastTapRef check gates it), but 'single-click MUST NOT toggle like' relies on this subtle timing. Verified via test (0 → 0 on single click, 0 → 1 on dblclick), but consider gating with an explicit onDoubleClick-only handler to eliminate any race on slow devices.
ExplorePage & HashtagPage: hashtag/trending pages never show a loading skeleton for the grid; empty state only shows after fetch completes. Consider a shared loading state.

StoriesRibbon hides the file input inside a <label> wrapper — works, but e2e selectors should target input[type='file'] scoped to [data-testid='create-story-modal'] (I used this — documented for future testers).
Pre-existing webpack warning about missing 'isOwnProfile' useEffect dep in ProfilePage (per main agent note) — not blocking, but worth cleaning.

success_rate.backend: 100% (5/5 sanity endpoints: GET /api/stories/feed, GET /api/explore, GET /api/hashtags/trending, GET /api/hashtags/test/posts, POST /api/stories — all 200)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (11/11 flows: stories-ribbon, create-story-modal+upload+toast, story-viewer+close, 5-item bottom nav with Explore replacing Products, explore-page+grid+trending chips, trending→/hashtag/:tag, inline hashtag links in post content, /hashtag/:tag page, double-tap-to-like heart animation + no-single-click-like, feed-explore-shortcut, quick-products in Profile Quick Access, Auto-badge conditional renders correctly — 0 badges for non-auto posts as expected)

test_credentials: Created ad-hoc during run via /api/auth/progressive-signup + /api/auth/complete-profile (pattern: e2e_a_<ts>@test.com, e2e_b_<ts>@test.com, Test123!). Admin password per /app/memory/test_credentials.md: NetworkCapital2025!.
seed_data_creation: Seeded 1 post containing '#test #networkcapital hello' with a 1x1 PNG image, and 4+ image stories across 4 test users. All visible in ribbon, explore grid, trending chips (#test, #networkcapital) and on /hashtag/test + /hashtag/networkcapital pages.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Prefer direct API token injection (localStorage.setItem('token', <jwt>)) over driving the AuthPage — the AuthPage uses phone-first signup which is awkward to script. StoriesRibbon.load() fetches on mount only — when opening a story modal to upload, wait ~3s after set_input_files(...) before asserting toast+modal close. /api/stories/feed returns ALL non-expired stories sitewide (no follow gating), so any seeded user's stories show up for a fresh account. Progressive signup response field is 'token' not 'access_token' (confirmed again).
rca of the issue: No production bugs found. The only transient observation: in one earlier playwright pass, [data-testid^='story-'] was empty when the feed was loaded with wait_for_timeout(4000). A 7000ms wait consistently surfaced all 4 story groups, and a programmatic read of document.querySelectorAll showed the DOM render happens after an axios fetch resolves — so this was a test-timing artifact, not a product bug. Mitigation: future tests should await the ribbon fetch either by waiting for a specific story-<user_id> selector or by spying on the /api/stories/feed response.
